newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPOs-Public sector mobilisation up sharply.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPOs-Public sector mobilisation up sharply.

text.p: The Indian government has monopolised resource mobilisation from the primary capital market after investors lost faith in the private sector in the last two financial years, Prime Database said on Monday.

The public sector's share of the total mobilisation through public issues in 1994/95 was a miniscule 9 percent at 12.5 billion rupees, according to Prime, the country's premier data base on the primary capital market.
This rose sharply to 43 percent in 1995/96 at 50.59 billion rupees and to a high 65 percent in 1996/97 at 75.39 billion rupees.

Of the total 99.17 billion rupees mobilised through debt public issues in the 1995/96 to 1996/97 2-year period, the public sector accounted for a significant 87 percent at 86.27 billion rupees, Prime said.

Debt mobilisation through public issues in the 2-year period has been from IDBI (26 billion rupees), ICICI (24.9 billion rupees), IFCI (12.37 billion rupees), IRFC (7.5 billion rupees), SCICI (5 billion rupees), Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam (3 billion rupees), Maharashtra Krishna Valley (3 billion rupees), HUDCO (2.5 billion rupees) and Konkan Railway (2 billion rupees).
On the equity front, the public sector's share has been comparatively lower, though it is now on the increase.

Of the total 135.53 billion rupees mobilised through equity public issues in the 2 year period, the public sector's share has risen to 29 percent at 39.71 billion rupees and could rise to over 50 percent in the current fiscal 1997/98 according to Prime's estimates.

In the preceding 2-year period, public equity issues have been floated by IDBI (19.35 billion rupees), Bank of Baroda (8.5 billion rupees), Bank of India (6.75 billion rupees), TNPL (2.2 billion rupees), Dena Bank (1.8 billion rupees), GSFC (470 million rupees), Optel (440 million rupees), and HFC (200 million rupees).

During 1994/95, there was no debt mobilisation by the public sector though an amount of 12.51 billion rupees had been raised through equity issues: Hindustan Petroleum (4.61 billion rupees), Oriental Bank (3.6 billion rupees), LIC Housing Finance (1.14 billion rupees), Punjab Communications (1.05 billion rupees), Hindustan Organic Chemicals (570 million rupees), TFCI (510 million rupees), GIC Housing Finance (230 million rupees).
In addition, partly convertible debenture issues have been offered by Bharat Earth Movers (660 million rupees) and Balmer Lawrie (160 million rupees).

On the other hand, according to Prime, the private sector has now been having little success in equity mobilisation which has nosedived from 120.61 billion rupees in 1994/95 to 66.63 billion rupees in 1995/96 to only 29.19 billion rupees in 1996/97.
The investors' loss of faith in the private sector, after having incurred huge losses in the 1992/94 period, is the major reason for this sector's plight.
As far as mobilisation through private placement of debt is concerned, Haldea states the government's share in resource mobilisation is even more pronounced.

In 1995/96, of the total such placements of 99.64 billion rupees, the public sector had cornered 96 percent of 95.16 billion rupees. In 1996/97, the Government organisations mobilised 163.38 billion rupees or 90 percent of the total debt placements of 181.04 billion rupees.

A significant feature of resource mobilisation, through both public issues and private placements, has been the dominant role of the financial institutions and banks. As per the Prime study, their raisings have gone up from 101.95 billion rupees in 1995/96 which constituted 47 percent of the total mobilisation to 152.46 billion rupees in 1996/97, hogging a 51 percent share.

According to Prime, all forthcoming issues of any significant size are only from the Government sector. On the one hand, there are several public issues lined up from banks including ICICI Banking Corporation (1.43 billion rupees), Corporation Bank (3.04 billion rupees), UTI Bank (500 million rupees), Canara Bank (7.0 billion rupees), IDBI Bank (1.5 billion rupees), Punjab & Sind Bank (8 billion rupees) and Vijaya Bank (3.6 billion rupees).

In addition, issues are also in the offing of all the SBI subsidiaries: State Bank of Travancore, State Bank of Indore, State Bank of Mysore, State Bank of Saurashtra, State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur, State Bank of Hyderabad and State Bank of Patiala.

There are proposed issues from several PSUs including HUDCO, MTNL, Numaligarh Refinary, Bharat Petroleum, Maharashtra Krishna Valley, Shipping Corporation, Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam, SBI Capital Markets and Gujarat Mineral. On the horizon also are mega disinvestment exercises from VSNL, Container Corporation and GAIL, among others.
